chainA.label: Shared commercial identity/versioning foundation
chainA.selectionReason: Tied on unlockScore with Product IDs. Chosen because a real 'product/version manifest' (required behavioral proof: deterministic manifest generation) naturally combines BOTH a SKU-safe product identifier AND a semver version in one document, so this feature's real implementation covers the full required-proof list (valid/invalid product identifiers, semver comparison, compatibility decisions, manifest generation) rather than only half of it. Product IDs alone would not have covered semver comparison/compatibility; Versioning alone naturally extends to cover product-id validation as part of the manifest.

chainB.label: Offline license verification or trial/entitlement state (pick higher-unlock)
chainB.selectionReason: Tied on unlockScore with Offline Trial. Chosen as more foundational: Chain C's own 'licensed' trial state (per the mission's own Chain-C description) is naturally defined in terms of 'does a valid signed license exist', so License Verification is a logical prerequisite for a future Trial/Entitlement batch to build on, not the reverse. Offline Trial State is deferred to a future batch, not abandoned.

chainC_verticalSlice.pipelineStages: INPUT (a user-supplied WAV file, real PCM data, generated in-test — never sourced/commercial content) -> VALIDATION (real WAV/PCM structural checks reusing the Batch-2 Studio decodeWav-equivalent logic, reimplemented locally per this task's own file-ownership boundary) -> METADATA EXTRACTION (duration, sample rate, channel count) -> SHA256 INVENTORY (content-hash based dedup/provenance) -> CATALOG ENTRY (mapping record) -> ATOMIC SAVE (Batch 1's AtomicSave) -> CLOSE/REOPEN -> MISSING-SOURCE RECOVERY (source file deleted after ingestion; catalog entry must detect and report, not silently succeed) -> MANIFEST OUTPUT (deterministic catalog manifest, integrating with Chain A's version-manifest primitive).
